title.narrative: Zambia: Livestock Development and Animal Health Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Livestock Development and Animal Health Project is to improve the productivity of key livestock production systems for targeted female and male smallholder producers in selected areas of the recipient's territory. The project will have three components. The first component of the project is livestock services provision. The objectives of this component are to: 1) strengthen the zoonotic and contagious animal diseases surveillance and control systems, including laboratory diagnostic capacities; 2) build institutional capacity within the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MoAL) to improve service delivery; and 3) improve the capacity to monitor food safety of facilities in the targeted project areas. The second component of the project is productive on-farm investments. The objective of this component is to improve productivity of identified production systems through grant support to on-farm investments. The third component of the project is project management. The objective of this component is to ensure efficient and timely delivery of project resources in accordance with its objectives.
To contribute to the improvement of livestock health and production of selected smallholder systems in targeted areas of the Recipient's territory.

title.narrative: Increase in livestock production in project areas measured by:

comment.narrative: Average number of village chickens/goats/reared pigs per SHH: “End of Project Evaluation and Beneficiary Assessment” draft report provide some estimates (respectively 30, 16 and 11 for chickens, goats and reared pigs, and 2.1 Litres for milk per cow par day). However, this information has some problems: (i) EoP values of the draft Beneficiary Assessment are specific to project areas whilst Baseline and Target values were based on the “Rural Agricultural Livelihoods Survey (RALS) 2012 and 2015 data which provide provincial values; (ii) Indicator: number of animals owned by SHH cannot specifically be attributed to project activities: the determining factors of the number of animals per SHH are broader than the ones on which the project intervened; (iii) the EoP values of the indicators were already or mostly achieved when target values were determined (respectively 13.8, 7.3 and 6.2 for chickens, goats and reared pigs (RALS, 2015). Milk produced per SHH keeping cows per day (liters): Reliable Information is not available. Baseline and Target value referred to crossbred cows whose milk is collected through a Milk Collection Center (MCC) whilst the EoP draft report is referring to data collected in average SHH with local breeds. The EoP Beneficiary Assessment shows lower average milk production compared to the 2016's Beneficiaries Assessment: 3.1 L per cows in 2016 against 2.1 L per cows in 2018. Furthermore, depending on the breed, the EoP is lower or not significantly higher than the project's baseline survey which showed 2 L/day for local cows and a 3.7L/day for all cows.

title.narrative: Disease incidence in the project areas measured by:

comment.narrative: FMD Outbreaks in cattle: End-of-Project (EoP) value is 1. This indicator is considered not achieved because of the SAT 3 strain which broke out in 2015 and resurfaced in another area in December 2017 when control measures were available under the project. The outbreak of a new strain of the virus has however, raised technical arguments as to why it should not be considered as a new disease since its control requires a different vaccine. Although the SAT 3 has been isolated in buffalo herds in Zambia, it had never occurred in cattle until this outbreak. District verifiably cleared of CBPP: Initial target (13) revised to 6 by ICR mission to consider ony districts targeted by the project. Indicator achieved.

This indicator was re-calculated to try to eliminate double/multiple counting of same SHH. Refer to Annex 9 for disaggregated data and estimation methodology. The same SHH could benefit from cattle vaccination for FMD, CBPP and ECF as well as vaccination for village chickens but should not be counted four times. This indicators achieved 85% success. Beneficiaries of animal vaccinations represented the largest majority of total beneficiaries: (i) vaccinations: 96.15% (with 84% of total beneficiaries of ND vaccination), (ii) Matching Grants: 3.77%, and (iii) Various trainings: 0.08%.

title.narrative: Vaccination coverage in project risk areas against:

comment.narrative: A livestock census has never been carried out in more that 10 years, therefore accurate animal population does not exist. Moreover, estimating bird population for free range chickens is particularly challenging. For newcastle disease in village chickens, reliabe data EoP is not available. CBPP in cattle: The project maintained a satisfactory rate of CBPP vaccination during all its implementation: 1 campaign conducted every year from 2013 to 2017 with an average of 342,000 animals vaccinated per campaign and a coverage against targeted population to be vaccinated of 86%. FMD in cattle: achieved considering average for bivalent vaccine: 8 campaigns conducted out of 11 possible with an average of 573,205 livestock vaccinated per campaign and a coverage against targeted vaccinatin by districts of 96% .

title.narrative: Utilization rate of the Livestock Improvement Grant Facility recipients that have implemented the projects:

comment.narrative: EoP target for this indicator (initially 70 and 30) revised to ensure that sum of the two gives 100%. Annual figures were to be disaggregated by gender of recipients (in case of POs choose gender more represented). However, utilization referred to disbursement for the intended purposes and not the utilization of the grant for the “intended purpose“.

title.narrative: Smallholder livestock owners satisfied by the quality of veterinary services supported by the project

comment.narrative: EoP values are based on the “End of Project Evaluation and Beneficiary Assessment” draft report (Sept. 2018) that provides results by species (cattle 43.2%; goats 47,8%, pigs 42.1%, local chickens 35.6%). The average value between species has been considered. To be noted that the indicator showed a better value in project's areas compared to control (35.3%)

title.narrative: Food Safety surveillance and monitoring plans are developed and implemented by MFL

comment.narrative: Indicator is partially achieved for the plans that have been developed: The two documents produced covering these diseases/issues are still in draft form. Some laboratory analyses continue to be carried out as was the case at project start but these analyses are not based on plans prepared.

title.narrative: Number of client days of training deliverd to MFL staff:

comment.narrative: Indicator partially achieved. Annual figures not disaggregated by gender.

title.narrative: Smallholder livestock owners in project areas adopting at least one recommended practice in improved animal husbandry:

comment.narrative: Original target was 48,000 (number). Reliable information for this indicator is not available: “End of Project Evaluation and Beneficiary Assessment” assessed the criteria but with reference to animal vaccination/immunizations. However, husbandry practices to be considered for this indicator were: (i) better herd management including herd registration (ii) implementation of a herd health plan; (iii) access to improved genetic material including AI; (iv) improved animal feeding, fodder, feeding supplement; and (v) improved habitat. Project did not provide formal evidence in relation to the adoption of these practices. The Beneficiary Assessment survey does not address this indicator.

title.narrative: Specimen Samples tested in laboratories supported by the project of :

comment.narrative: Overall indicators could be considered as achieved for CBPP and FMD. For ND, testing was conducted only as part of a study to measure the efficacy of the vaccine and not routinely, and was not reported.

title.narrative: Livestock infrastructure constructed or rehabilitated by the project

comment.narrative: The original target was for tier 1&1+ 157, for tier two 26 and for tier three 2. This was reduced to only 11 including two tier 3 and nine tier 2. The rest were transferred to the demand driven matching grant component. This indicator was partially achieved: The following infrastructure were completed at project close: one Tier 3, seven Tier 2, and a peri-urban livestock market. The infrastucture has been completed but not officially handed over by the contractors to the Ministry. This indicator was revised following the December 2015 restructuring.

title.narrative: Action plan for genetic resources is developed and implemented. "Developed" refers to the approval by DVS. "Implemented" refers to >10% annual budget utilization.

comment.narrative: This indicator is partially achieved. The document is prepared and cleared but no evidence of implementation. Furthermore, the document prepared is not an actions plan and does not propose any budgeted investment plan. The Report provides a structure/basis for developing a National Plan of Action by providing strategic priority areas for the Action Plan and measures for each strategic prioity area. In addition a structure for the National early warning and response system for determining endangered indigenous Animal Genetic Resources has been outlined.

title.narrative: Zambia Animal Health and Production Information Management System developed and functional

M/E system established and functional; "Established" refers to the definition of the methodology for all project indicators. "Functional" refers to > 80% data collection/analysis of project indicators

comment.narrative: This indicator is partially achieved: The M&E has been rated modest in this ICR team. Overall, data was collected but with gaps and inaccuracies. At project close, there was no updated database for the 600+ matching grants approved. through LDAHP.
